note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Status of Accounting Standards and Scope of Applicability
explain: Standards are formulated by the ASB and issued by the ICAI Council.
Central Government notifies Accounting Standards for corporate entities through MCA.
Accounting standards cannot override laws or local statutory regulations.
They apply to any enterprise doing commercial, industrial, or business activities.
Even charitable or religious trusts follow AS if running any commercial activity.
Enterprises solely doing non-commercial acts, like flood relief donations, are excluded.
Management holds the duty to prepare statements and make proper disclosures.
Statutory auditors must examine and report compliance under Section 143(3)(e).
Standards apply only to items that are material by nature or amount.
Materiality depends on information content; e.g., a small statutory penalty is material.

flow.title: Three-Step Test for Applicability of AS
steps: Check if AS applies to enterprise
Check if AS applies to statement
Check if AS applies to item
Evaluate materiality of financial item
Apply standard and disclose deviations

topics.example: A charitable hospital running a commercial pharmacy must apply Accounting Standards to all its operations, including charitable patient wards.
remember: Section 129(1): Companies must present accounts matching AS notified under Section 133.
Section 143(3)(e): Auditor must report whether accounts comply with AS.
Section 129(5): Deviations, reasons, and financial effects must be disclosed.
Materiality is judged on information relevance, not just monetary size.
mistakes: Believing non-profit or charitable organisations never have to follow Accounting Standards.
Assuming small value items like penalties for breach of law are immaterial because of low amount.

quiz.q: Under which section of the Companies Act, 2013 must an auditor report compliance with Accounting Standards?
quiz.why: Section 143(3)(e) specifically mandates the auditor to report whether the company complies with notified AS.

quiz.q: An entity is exempted from Accounting Standards only if:
o: It is established for charitable purposes
No part of its activity is commercial, industrial, or business
Its turnover is less than rupees one crore
It operates as a non-corporate partnership firm
quiz.why: Exclusion applies only when no part of the entity's activity is commercial, industrial, or business in nature.

topics.title: Accounting Standards and Income Computation and Disclosure Standards (ICDS)
explain: Accounting Standards ensure transparency and comparability in commercial financial statements.
Allowable expenses and tax exemptions depend strictly on government fiscal tax laws.
Charging an expense in profit and loss does not guarantee income tax deduction.
Central Government notifies ICDS under Section 145(2) for income computation.
Applies to mercantile assessees computing business income or income from other sources.
Individuals and HUFs not covered under tax audit of Section 44AB are exempt from ICDS.
There are ten notified ICDS operational starting from Assessment Year 2017-18.

flow.title: ICDS Applicability Test
steps: Check income head: Business or Other Sources
Confirm assessee follows mercantile accounting system
Check if non-audit Individual or HUF
Apply 10 notified ICDS for tax

topics.example: A finance lease asset is depreciated in the lessee's books as per AS 19, but tax depreciation is claimed only by the lessor as legal owner.
remember: Section 145(2) empowers Central Government to notify ICDS.
10 ICDS exist and took effect from Assessment Year 2017-18.
ICDS is strictly for tax computation, not for maintaining statutory books.
mistakes: Confusing ICDS with AS by trying to use ICDS to prepare standard balance sheets.
Thinking tax exemption under Section 10 allows omitting revenue recognition from commercial financial statements.

quiz.q: How many Income Computation and Disclosure Standards (ICDS) have been notified under Section 145(2)?
quiz.why: The Central Government has notified ten ICDS for computation of business and other source income.

quiz.q: From which Assessment Year did the ten notified ICDS become applicable?
quiz.why: ICDS became operational for computation of taxable income starting from Assessment Year 2017-18.

topics.title: Classification Criteria for Non-Company Entities
explain: ICAI classifies non-corporate entities into Level I, Level II, Level III, and Level IV.
Level I are large, Level II are medium, Level III are small, and Level IV are micro.
Level II, III, and IV non-corporate entities are jointly referred to as MSMEs.
Classification is evaluated at the close of the relevant financial accounting period.
Level I: Listed entities, banks, financial institutions, insurers, or holding/subsidiary thereof.
Level I: Turnover over rupees 250 crores or borrowings over rupees 50 crores in preceding year.
Level II: Preceding turnover between rupees 50 and 250 crores, or borrowings between 10 and 50 crores.
Level III: Preceding turnover between rupees 10 and 50 crores, or borrowings between 2 and 10 crores.
Level IV: All other non-corporate entities not covered under Levels I, II, or III.
Two-consecutive-year rule: Dropping from a higher level requires qualifying for two straight years before getting relief.

flow.title: Non-Company Entity Level Classification
steps: Check listing status, bank, or insurance business
Test turnover > ₹250 cr or borrowings > ₹50 cr
If yes to either, classify as Level I
Test turnover > ₹50 cr or borrowings > ₹10 cr: Level II
Test turnover > ₹10 cr or borrowings > ₹2 cr: Level III
All remaining entities classify as Level IV

topics.example: A partnership firm with borrowings of ₹12 crores and turnover of ₹8 crores is classified as Level II because borrowings exceed ₹10 crores.
remember: Level I: Turnover > ₹250 cr OR Borrowings > ₹50 cr at any time.
Level II: Turnover > ₹50 cr to ₹250 cr OR Borrowings > ₹10 cr to ₹50 cr.
Level III: Turnover > ₹10 cr to ₹50 cr OR Borrowings > ₹2 cr to ₹10 cr.
Level IV: Turnover <= ₹10 cr AND Borrowings <= ₹2 cr.
Holdings and subsidiaries take the higher classification category.
Two consecutive years of lower status needed to claim lower-level relaxations.
mistakes: Checking both turnover and borrowings together with 'AND' instead of 'OR' for higher classification.
Forgetting that borrowings threshold includes public deposits and applies at any time during the previous year.

quiz.q: A non-corporate entity having borrowings of rupees 3 crores and turnover of rupees 8 crores is classified as:
quiz.why: Borrowings exceed rupees 2 crores but do not exceed rupees 10 crores, making it a Level III entity.

quiz.q: When an entity shifts from Level I to Level II, how long must it stay in the lower status before availing exemptions?
quiz.why: An entity must cease to be covered in Level I for two consecutive years before availing lower level relaxations.

topics.title: Exemptions and Applicability of AS to Non-Company Entities
explain: Level I non-corporate entities must comply in full with all Accounting Standards.
AS 3 (Cash Flow), AS 17 (Segment), and AS 20 (EPS) do not apply to Levels II, III, and IV.
AS 14 does not apply to Level IV unless they enter into an amalgamation transaction.
AS 18 (Related Party) and AS 24 (Discontinuing Operations) do not apply to Levels III and IV.
AS 28 (Impairment) does not apply to Level IV; Levels II and III get value-in-use estimate relaxations.
AS 21, AS 23, AS 25, and AS 27 do not mandate presenting consolidated or interim reports.
AS 22 applies to Level IV only for current tax provisions; deferred tax asset/liability is adjusted to reserves.
AS 15 provides tiered relaxations based on whether staff headcount is below 50 or 50 and above.
Entities availing exemptions must disclose their MSME level and compliance details in financial notes.

flow.title: Non-Company Exemption Check
steps: Identify entity classification level
Exclude AS 3, 17, and 20 for MSMEs
Exclude AS 18 and AS 24 if Level III or IV
Exclude AS 14 and AS 28 if Level IV
Apply simplified AS 15, 19, 22, 28, 29
Add mandatory disclosure notes in statements

topics.example: A Level IV partnership firm does not prepare a Cash Flow Statement (AS 3) and only accounts for current tax without calculating deferred tax under AS 22.
remember: AS 3, AS 17, and AS 20 are completely not applicable to Level II, III, and IV entities.
AS 18 and AS 24 are inapplicable to Level III and Level IV.
Level IV entities apply AS 22 only for current tax, adjusting accumulated deferred tax into opening revenue reserves.
AS 15 distinguishes between entities having 50 or more employees vs fewer than 50 employees.
mistakes: Thinking Level II entities are exempt from AS 18 (Related Party Disclosures); AS 18 is mandatory for Level II.
Failing to disclose the specific accounting standards where relaxations have been availed in the notes.

quiz.q: Which of the following standards is applicable to Level II non-corporate entities but not applicable to Level III entities?
quiz.why: AS 18 applies to Level II entities but is completely non-applicable to Level III and Level IV entities.

quiz.q: How does a non-corporate Level IV entity account for deferred tax under AS 22?
o: Computes deferred tax using standard rates
Is fully exempted and only accounts for current tax
Computes deferred tax once every two years
Recognises deferred tax directly in profit or loss
quiz.why: Level IV entities apply AS 22 only for current tax provisions and are exempt from deferred tax accounting.

topics.title: Criteria for Classification of Companies (SMC vs Non-SMC)
explain: Corporate entities under AS Rules are classified into two groups: SMCs and Non-SMCs.
An SMC has no listed equity or debt securities and is not in the process of listing.
An SMC cannot be a bank, financial institution, or insurance company.
Turnover excluding other income cannot exceed rupees 250 crores in the preceding year.
Borrowings including public deposits cannot exceed rupees 50 crores at any time in the preceding year.
An SMC cannot be a holding or subsidiary of an entity that is not an SMC.
Status conditions must be verified at the end of the relevant accounting period.
Companies failing any single SMC condition are categorized as Non-SMCs.
A Non-SMC becoming an SMC must stay an SMC for two consecutive accounting periods to claim relaxations.

flow.title: SMC Eligibility Verification
steps: Check unlisted status in and outside India
Verify company is not bank, FI, or insurer
Confirm preceding turnover <= ₹250 crores
Confirm borrowings <= ₹50 crores at all times
Confirm parent/subsidiary are also SMCs
Classify as SMC or Non-SMC

topics.example: A private company with ₹40 crore turnover and ₹2 crore borrowings whose holding company has ₹300 crore turnover is a Non-SMC because its parent is a Non-SMC.
remember: SMC Turnover limit: Does not exceed ₹250 crores.
SMC Borrowings limit: Does not exceed ₹50 crores at any time.
Neither listed nor in process of listing anywhere.
Cannot be a holding or subsidiary of a Non-SMC.
2 consecutive periods rule applies when transitioning from Non-SMC to SMC.
mistakes: Considering other income while calculating the turnover ceiling of ₹250 crores.
Allowing a company that just dropped below limits in year 1 to instantly claim SMC exemptions without waiting for the two-year period.

quiz.q: What is the maximum turnover limit (excluding other income) for a company to qualify as an SMC?
quiz.why: Under Rule 2(e), turnover excluding other income must not exceed rupees 250 crores in the preceding year.

quiz.q: A company classified as Non-SMC in 20X1-X2 qualifies on limits as an SMC in 20X2-X3. Can it avail SMC exemptions in 20X2-X3?
o: Yes, because it meets limits on the balance sheet date
No, it must remain an SMC for two consecutive accounting periods
Yes, if approved by the board of directors
No, it must wait for five consecutive periods
quiz.why: A non-SMC becoming an SMC cannot avail exemptions until it remains an SMC for two consecutive accounting periods.

topics.title: Applicability and Exemptions of AS for Companies (SMC vs Non-SMC)
explain: Non-SMCs must comply with all Accounting Standards in their complete entirety.
AS 17 (Segment Reporting) is entirely not applicable to Small and Medium Sized Companies.
SMCs are exempt from disclosing diluted EPS under AS 20 (both including and excluding extraordinary items).
AS 28 allows SMCs to determine 'value in use' via reasonable estimate instead of present value techniques.
AS 15 gives SMCs relaxations regarding short-term absences, long-term discounting, and actuarial plans.
AS 19 and AS 29 grant specific disclosure exemptions to SMCs.
AS 25 (Interim Financial Reporting) applies only if a company elects or is legally directed to report interim numbers.
SMCs availing relaxations must include a clear disclosure note affirming their SMC status.

flow.title: Corporate Standard Implementation Flow
steps: Identify company as SMC or Non-SMC
Non-SMC applies all AS fully
SMC omits AS 17 in entirety
SMC omits diluted EPS disclosure in AS 20
Apply simplified value in use under AS 28
Insert SMC compliance disclosure in notes

topics.example: An unlisted trading company classified as an SMC reports basic EPS on its statement of profit and loss, but legally omits diluted EPS calculations and Segment Reporting.
remember: AS 17 is the only AS completely inapplicable to SMCs in its entirety.
AS 20 diluted EPS disclosure is exempted for SMCs.
AS 28 value in use can be based on reasonable estimate without discounting.
Mandatory note: 'The Company is an SMC as defined in Companies (AS) Rules, 2021...'
mistakes: Believing AS 3 (Cash Flow Statement) is exempt for all SMCs under AS rules; AS 3 is applicable to SMC companies unless exempt under Section 2(40) for One Person / Small Companies.
Omitting basic EPS disclosure for SMCs; only diluted EPS disclosure is exempt under AS 20.

quiz.q: Which Accounting Standard is entirely not applicable to Small and Medium Sized Companies (SMCs)?
quiz.why: AS 17 (Segment Reporting) is completely not applicable to SMCs in its entirety.

quiz.q: Under AS 20, what specific exemption is granted to an SMC?
o: Exemption from presenting EPS on face of Profit & Loss
Exemption from disclosure of Diluted EPS
quiz.why: Disclosure of diluted earnings per share (both including and excluding extraordinary items) is exempted for SMCs.
